facts: Unfortunately, your claim for home treatment is not covered under your policy.
The audit found the clause does not clearly establish the ground given.

cited_clauses.quote: Medical Treatment should be rendered from a registered Medical Practitioner who holds a valid practicing license in respect of such AYUSH Treatments; and Such treatment taken is within the jurisdiction of India; and Clause 4.2 (12) under Permanent Exclusions, is superseded to the extent covered under this Benefit.

The Company will indemnify the Insured Person, only through Reimbursement Facility, up to the Sum Insured ,as specified in the Policy Schedule, for the Medical Expenses incurred towards Domiciliary Hospitalization, i.e., Coverage extended when Medically Necessary treatment is taken at home (as explained in Definition 2.1.14), subject to the conditions specified below:

reasoning: The policy clause does not clearly establish that home treatments are covered, and Clause 4.2 (12) under Permanent Exclusions explicitly excludes home treatments.
relief_sought: Please clarify the ground for the rejection and explain how home treatments are covered under the policy.
document_checklist: Copy of the claim rejection letter
Medical bills, prescriptions and investigation reports
Earlier correspondence with the insurer, including any grievance acknowledgement
deadline_note: A complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman needs a written representation to the insurer first; it must then be made within one year of the insurer's rejection, or of one month after the representation was sent (Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, Rule 14(3), checked against the published text as amended till 09.11.2023; later amendments not checked). Confirm with the Ombudsman office before relying on a date, and compute dates with the deadline tool.
